name: Kemusan (科目三)
blurb: The "Subject Three" dance from Guangxi, China: a hand-flicking craze of late 2023
title: Kemusan (科目三): The "Subject Three" Dance from China Explained
description: Kemusan (科目三, "Subject Three") is a dance from Guangxi, China, set to a DJ remix of 一笑江湖. It went viral on Douyin in late 2023, then spread worldwide on TikTok.
h1: What is the Kemusan (Subject Three) dance?
answer: Kemusan (科目三, kēmù sān, "Subject Three") is a dance craze from Guangxi in southern China: fast hand and wrist flicks, knees swinging side to side, twisting hips and small shuffling steps, usually set to a DJ remix of the Chinese song 一笑江湖 (Yi Xiao Jiang Hu). The name borrows the third part of China's driving test, after a joke that people from Guangxi must pass three "subjects": singing folk songs, eating rice noodles and dancing. It took off on Douyin in October 2023, exploded when Haidilao hot pot waiters started performing it in November, and spread abroad on TikTok by December.

body: There is no single official routine. The core moves are rapid flicks of the hands and wrists, knees swinging outward, a twisting waist and hips, and quick small steps on a bouncy beat. The track, 一笑江湖, began as a Chinese folk-style song with opera-like vocals; a sped-up DJ remix became the dance's signature sound.

Several origin stories circulate. The most common says a young man from Guangxi first danced it to liven up a friend's wedding reception, and it moved from there to bars and short-video apps. Who actually started it is not settled.

ul: Asking for a performance: "来一段科目三！" (Give us some Subject Three!)
Praising a smooth dancer: "That's a perfect score on Subject Three."
Driving-test jokes: "I can't even pass Subject One, never mind Subject Three."
Comment-section code: "Have you passed Subject Three?" means "Can you do the dance?"

body.note: Not everyone loved it: during the Haidilao craze some diners found it disruptive, and doctors warned that over-enthusiastic knee swings can cause injuries.

body: Kemusan peaked from late 2023 to early 2024, and newer novelty dances with similar moves soon followed, so it is now a well-known older trend. The name is still instantly recognized, and it still turns up at weddings, office parties and gatherings, where "passing Subject Three" means you can do the dance.

faq.q: What song is the Subject Three dance set to?
faq.a: Usually a DJ remix of 一笑江湖 (Yi Xiao Jiang Hu), a Chinese folk-style song credited to 闻人听書. The fast remix became the dance's standard soundtrack.

faq.q: Why is it called Subject Three?
faq.a: 科目三 is the road-driving part of China's driving test. A popular joke says people from Guangxi face three tests in life: Subject One is singing folk songs, Subject Two is eating rice noodles and Subject Three is dancing.

faq.q: How do you do the Kemusan dance?
faq.a: Flick your hands and wrists back and forth quickly, swing your knees from side to side, twist at the waist and hips, and take small quick steps, all on the beat. The moves are simple, but go easy on your knees.
